thread:
dinesh: Seeing a sudden CUDA OOM on gpu-47 even though headroom shows ~1.9GB free. Pushing this here because the autoscaler didn't react and jobs are failing. 

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created (auto-detect) — type: GPU OOM spike. Severity: P2. Runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/gpu-oom

ben: @dinesh can you paste the root log + the headroom snapshot? Any recent deploys to that node?

carla: I pulled the node metrics, tagging in a few graphs. Noted KV cache reservations spiking prior to OOM. Could be reserve shrink/compaction race.

alice: Quick note — we saw a similar pattern last month where the allocator triggered a reserve shrink during a microburst and fragmentation made the free blocks unusable, causing OOM despite "headroom" numbers. Worth checking reserved-block map.

dinesh: paste logs and samples: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:21:03Z] model-server[pid=3121]: Allocator::reserve: reserved=4.0GB headroom=1.9GB
[2026-03-15T18:21:04Z] model-server[pid=3121]: KVCache: pinned_blocks=12 free_blocks=3
[2026-03-15T18:21:05Z] model-server[pid=3121]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 384MB
[2026-03-15T18:21:05Z] kernel: Out of memory: GPU 0 unable to allocate
```

And headroom report: `rictl node inspect gpu-47 --headroom` => `total_free=1.9GB reserved=4GB allocatable=6GB`

carla: Running `nvidia-smi` on the node shows some processes holding pinned pages from previous tasks (ghost allocations). Also see many small free segments -> fragmentation.

ben: Ok. Immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon+drain node and move new traffic off it, 2) force slab compaction/restart of model-server process (fast but disruptive), 3) tweak runtime env to disable reserve shrink or reduce reserve size. Which do we want first?

sre-oncall: Customer impact: 3 customers reporting error spikes on latency-sensitive endpoints. Rate of failed requests ~3-7/min. No broad outage but some degraded SLAs. Paging customer success to inform them — @carla can you assemble the customer list?

carla: On it. Sending PMs to the three customer owners now.

alice: For the runtime tweak: we can set REDWOOD_ALLOC_RESERVE_RATIO=0.6 (currently 0.4) to avoid aggressive shrink behavior for the short-term. Alternative is `REDWOOD_DISABLE_RESERVE_SHRINK=true` which prevents compaction that causes fragmentation thrash. I prefer disable-shrink for a short window while we evacuate the node.

dinesh: I can apply the env change and restart just model-server on this pod. That should be a quick flip: `kubectl set env deployment/model-server REDWOOD_DISABLE_RESERVE_SHRINK=true -n inference && kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-server -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-47`

ben: If we restart pods only on that node we still risk eviction churn. I'd rather cordon the node and fail traffic to other healthy nodes, then rotate workloads back. Do we have spare capacity?

carla: cluster spare capacity is ~20% in this AZ. We can route traffic to dedicated pool (fallback-model-small) for the bursty requests: add a routing rule in the console or flip the feature flag to use a smaller quantized variant. That will lower memory usage.

incident-bot: Update — paging oncall: @sre-oncall received the page. Playbook step 2 initiated (isolate node).

sre-oncall: I'm on it. Cordon + drain in progress: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-47
kubectl drain gpu-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

dinesh: While drain runs, I executed a live diagnostic: `procmap --node gpu-47 --alloc-table` => shows many tiny reserved blocks < 64KB and a small number of pinned large blocks that are not reclaimable. Looks like allocator fragmentation + reserved-block shrink left unusable holes.

alice: That matches. Also seeing logs where `Reserve::shrink()` called just before the OOM. Suggest we avoid shrink for 30 minutes, let drain finish, then restart node-level daemons to compact memory.

ben: Agreed. SRE: proceed with cordon/drain. dinesh and alice — prepare a rollback if restart doesn't free up. Carla — keep customers notified. I'll update incident channel with status and doc link.

carla: Customer comms sent: short note, we're mitigating and will follow up with timeline.

sre-oncall: Drain completed. Pods rescheduled to other nodes. Observability: error rate dropped to ~0.5/min now. No new OOMs on gpu-47 after eviction, but node still shows fragmented reservations.

dinesh: I pulled a heap/profile dump from the model-server before it terminated. Attaching key snippet: 
```
AllocatorState:
  reserved_blocks: 4096
  free_chunks: 128  (mostly small < 64KB)
  pinned_chunks: 24 (total 2.1GB)
  compaction_last_called: 2026-03-15T18:20:58Z
```

alice: Next steps: 1) add a short-term runtime flag change to avoid reserve shrinking on all model-servers for 1 hour, 2) add a transient routing rule to prefer quantized/low-memory variants for latency-tier traffic, 3) schedule a postmortem and allocator investigation (fragmentation patterns, reserve shrink heuristics).

ben: I'll own the postmortem and prioritize a follow-up with allocator team. dinesh — please collect the heap dumps and the exact `Reserve::shrink()` call traces and upload to the incident artifact bucket.

dinesh: Uploading now to s3://redwood-incidents/2512345678/heapdumps.tar.gz

incident-bot: Severity update -> remains P2. Actions: node isolated, traffic rerouted, customers notified. See runbook step 4 for postmortem template.

carla: Quick telemetry note for later: add a probe to measure contiguous free segment sizes (not just total headroom) — that'll help differentiate fragmentation vs true headroom. File: https://go/redwood/infra/probes/contig-free-size

sre-oncall: Confirming customer-facing degradation resolved for now. I'll keep the node cordoned until allocator fix is rolled (or until scheduled maintenance).

ben: Summary for incident channel: Root cause suspected allocator reserve-shrink compaction race causing fragmentation -> GPU OOM despite reported headroom. Mitigations applied: node cordoned/drained, runtime flag to disable reserve shrink on the node (and planning cluster-wide short toggle), traffic routed to smaller model variants. Next: alloc-team deep-dive, add contiguity telemetry, postmortem.

alice: I'll open a Jira for the allocator bug with the traces and suggested mitigations.

dinesh: Thanks all. If anything spikes again I will re-open page.

carla: Closing loop with customers in 30m with root-cause update.

ben: Great work. Marking incident as mitigated. We'll run the postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
